content.text:
The verifier feedback this round is affirming on every substantive point: the compliant classification, the no-redline/no-comment output, the accurate characterisation of p0001, the non-probative nature of the failed deterministic check, and the handling of the Exhibit risk as a note. There is no defect left to correct — the only "failure" is a check that is structurally unsatisfiable because no audit clause exists to carry a frequency cap.

I'll resubmit the finding unchanged in substance, with the rationale leading on the dispositive point so the basis is unmistakable.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale:
Dispositive point: this Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection or verification right over the Customer, and imposes no record-keeping or self-reporting obligation on the Customer. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "records" and "books" each returned zero results across the single section (sec-preamble), and a full read of all 75 paragraphs confirms it.

The nearest "access" language is unrelated to verification: p0001 (quoted) is ordinary cooperation for service delivery; p0002 is the licence granted to Customer; p0025 restricts Customer from giving third parties access to the Service; p0035 and p0045 are database security representations. There is also nothing an audit right would police, since Impressions are "measured by Kubient" itself (p0009) and, under section 5, revenue flows from Kubient to Customer on a sequential-liability basis.

Direction: AUDIT constrains a Vendor-side right that burdens our party. The complete absence of that right leaves our audit exposure at nil, which is at least as favourable as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access). No walk-away trigger is present: no unlimited or unannounced audit right, and no Vendor remote access to Customer systems.

Compliant rather than missing: the rule does not expect a Customer-protective clause that we lack; it caps a Vendor right. Accordingly no redline and no counterparty comment is proposed, because inserting frequency, notice and cost limits would first have to create a Vendor audit right that does not exist today and would worsen our position.

Notes, not flagged as deviations: the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check cannot be met because there is no clause to bear a frequency cap. Forward-looking watch item only: section 1 defines Services by individual Exhibits and section 5 permits Exhibits to override the default fee mechanics, so if a future Exhibit introduces Customer-side reporting or a fee true-up, we should then negotiate the preferred limits, with the 15-day notice / 10% underpayment fallback available.
